sanskrit: bhṛśam āvrajamānasya tasyādhovāmalocanam prāsphurac cāskhalad rāmo vepathuś cāsya jāyate
english: As Rāma was hurrying back, his lower left eye twitched and throbbed, and a trembling came over him.

sanskrit: upālakṣya nimittāni so 'śubhāni muhur muhuḥ api kṣemaṃ tu sītāyā iti vai vyājahāra ha
english: Observing these ill omens again and again, he could only say, "May Sītā at least be well."

sanskrit: tvaramāṇo jagāmātha sītādarśanalālasaḥ śūnyam āvasathaṃ dṛṣṭvā babhūvodvignamānasaḥ
english: He hastened forward, longing to see Sītā, but upon finding the dwelling empty his heart was seized with anguish.

sanskrit: udbhramann iva vegena vikṣipan raghunandanaḥ tatra tatroṭajasthānam abhivīkṣya samantataḥ
english: The joy of the Raghus, as though frantic with urgency, roamed about searching everywhere around the site of the leaf hut.

sanskrit: dadarśa parṇaśālāṃ ca rahitāṃ sītayā tadā śriyā virahitāṃ dhvastāṃ hemante padminīm iva
english: He beheld the leaf cottage empty of Sītā, stripped of its beauty and in ruin, like a lotus pond in winter bereft of its glory.

sanskrit: rudantam iva vṛkṣaiś ca mlānapuṣpamṛgadvijam śriyā vihīnaṃ vidhvastaṃ saṃtyaktavanadaivatam
english: The trees seemed to weep, the flowers were withered, the deer and birds were still; the grove was desolate, stripped of its splendour, abandoned by its forest deities.

sanskrit: viprakīrṇājinakuśaṃ vipraviddhabṛsīkaṭam dṛṣṭvā śūnyoṭajasthānaṃ vilalāpa punaḥ punaḥ
english: Seeing the site of the hut empty, with the antelope-skin and kuśa grass scattered about and the woven mat tossed aside, he lamented again and again.

sanskrit: hṛtā mṛtā vā naṣṭā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati nilīnāpy atha vā bhīrur atha vā vanam āśritā
english: "Has she been abducted, or is she dead, or has she disappeared? Has she been devoured? Or perhaps the timid one is hiding somewhere, or has gone deep into the forest?"

sanskrit: gatā vicetuṃ puṣpāṇi phalāny api ca vā punaḥ atha vā padminīṃ yātā jalārthaṃ vā nadīṃ gatā
english: "Has she gone to gather flowers or fruits? Or has she gone to a lotus pond, or gone to the river for water?"

sanskrit: yatnān mṛgayamāṇas tu nāsasāda vane priyām śokaraktekṣaṇaḥ śokād unmatta iva lakṣyate
english: Though he searched diligently, he could not find his beloved in the forest; his eyes reddened with grief, he appeared as one driven mad by sorrow.

sanskrit: vṛkṣād vṛkṣaṃ pradhāvan sa girīṃś cāpi nadīn nadīm babhūva vilapan rāmaḥ śokapaṅkārṇavaplutaḥ
english: Running from tree to tree, from hill to hill, from river to river, Rāma lamented, plunged deep in the swamp-like ocean of grief.

sanskrit: asti kaccit tvayā dṛṣṭā sā kadambapriyā priyā kadamba yadi jānīṣe śaṃsa sītāṃ śubhānanām
english: "O Kadamba tree, have you seen her who loves the kadamba? If you know, tell me — tell me of Sītā of the fair face."

sanskrit: snigdhapallavasaṃkāśāṃ pītakauśeyavāsinīm śaṃsasva yadi vā dṛṣṭā bilva bilvopamastanī
english: "O Bilva tree, if you have seen her whose breasts resemble the bilva fruit, who is clad in yellow silk and whose complexion is like tender fresh shoots, then tell me."

sanskrit: atha vārjuna śaṃsa tvaṃ priyāṃ tām arjunapriyām janakasya sutā bhīrur yadi jīvati vā na vā
english: "Or you, O Arjuna tree, tell me of her who loves the arjuna — whether Janaka's timid daughter lives or not."

sanskrit: kakubhaḥ kakubhoruṃ tāṃ vyaktaṃ jānāti maithilīm latāpallavapuṣpāḍhyo bhāti hy eṣa vanaspatiḥ
english: "The kakubha tree surely knows that Maithilī whose thighs are like the kakubha — for it gleams rich with creeping shoots and blossoms."

sanskrit: bhramarair upagītaś ca yathā drumavaro hy ayam eṣa vyaktaṃ vijānāti tilakas tilakapriyām
english: "Surely this tilaka tree, best of trees hummed over by bees, knows her who loves the tilaka."

sanskrit: aśokaśokāpanuda śokopahatacetasaṃ tvannāmānaṃ kuru kṣipraṃ priyāsaṃdarśanena mām
english: "O Aśoka, remover of sorrow — quickly make me worthy of your name by showing me my beloved, for my heart is crushed by grief."

sanskrit: yadi tāla tvayā dṛṣṭā pakvatālaphalastanī kathayasva varārohāṃ kāruṣyaṃ yadi te mayi
english: "O Tāla tree, if you have seen her whose breasts are like ripe tāla fruit, if you have any compassion for me, then tell me of that fair-limbed one."

sanskrit: yadi dṛṣṭā tvayā sītā jambujāmbūnadaprabhā priyāṃ yadi vijānīṣe niḥśaṅkaṃ kathayasva me
english: "O Jambū tree, if you have seen Sītā whose radiance is like gold from the Jāmbūnada river, if you know my beloved, speak to me without hesitation."

sanskrit: atha vā mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ mṛga jānāsi maithilīm mṛgaviprekṣaṇī kāntā mṛgībhiḥ sahitā bhavet
english: "O deer, do you know Maithilī with eyes like a fawn? She who gazes like a doe — perhaps she is among your does."

sanskrit: gaja sā gajanāsorur yadi dṛṣṭā tvayā bhavet tāṃ manye viditāṃ tubhyam ākhyāhi varavāraṇa
english: "O elephant, if you have seen her whose thighs are like an elephant's trunk, I believe she is known to you — tell me, O noble bull elephant."

sanskrit: śārdūla yadi sā dṛṣṭā priyā candranibhānanā maithilī mama visrabdhaḥ kathayasva na te bhayam
english: "O tiger, if you have seen my beloved Maithilī whose face is like the moon, tell me freely — you have nothing to fear."

sanskrit: kiṃ dhāvasi priye nūnaṃ dṛṣṭāsi kamalekṣaṇe vṛkṣeṇācchādya cātmānaṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
english: "Why do you run, my beloved? Surely I see you, O lotus-eyed one — why do you hide yourself behind that tree and not speak to me?"

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha varārohe na te 'sti karuṇā mayi nātyarthaṃ hāsyaśīlāsi kimarthaṃ mām upekṣase
english: "Stop, stop, O fair-hipped one — have you no compassion for me? You are not given to excessive jesting — why then do you disregard me?"

sanskrit: pītakauśeyakenāsi sūcitā varavarṇini dhāvanty api mayā dṛṣṭā tiṣṭha yady asti sauhṛdam
english: "You are revealed by your yellow silk garment, O fair-complexioned one — even as you run I have seen you. Stop, if there is any affection between us."

sanskrit: naiva sā nūnam atha vā hiṃsitā cāruhāsinī kṛcchraṃ prāptaṃ hi māṃ nūnaṃ yathopekṣitum arhati
english: "No, it is not she — or else that lovely-smiling one has been slain; for surely the calamity that has befallen me warrants such utter disregard."

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ sā bhakṣitā bālā rākṣasaiḥ piśitāśanaiḥ vibhajyāṅgāni sarvāṇi mayā virahitā priyā
english: "Evidently the young one has been devoured by flesh-eating rākṣasas, her every limb dismembered — my beloved, bereft of me."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ tac chubhadantauṣṭhaṃ mukhaṃ niṣprabhatāṃ gatam sā hi campakavarṇābhā grīvā graiveya śobhitā
english: "Surely that face with its fair teeth and lips has lost its lustre; and that neck, radiant as the campaka flower and adorned with a necklace — gone."

sanskrit: komalā vilapantyās tu kāntāyā bhakṣitā śubhā nūnaṃ vikṣipyamāṇau tau bāhū pallavakomalau
english: "Surely those two tender arms, soft as young shoots, of my lamenting beloved — those lovely arms as she was being tossed about — have been devoured."

sanskrit: bhakṣitau vepamānāgrau sahastābharaṇāṅgadau mayā virahitā bālā rakṣasāṃ bhakṣaṇāya vai
english: "Those arms with their quivering fingertips, adorned with bracelets and armlets, have been devoured — the young one, separated from me, given over as food for rākṣasas."

sanskrit: sārtheneva parityaktā bhakṣitā bahubāndhavā hā lakṣmaṇa mahābāho paśyasi tvaṃ priyāṃ kva cit
english: "Abandoned as though by a merchant's caravan and devoured, she who had so many kinsmen — Ah, Lakṣmaṇa, O mighty-armed one, do you see my beloved anywhere?"

sanskrit: hā priye kva gatā bhadre hā sīteti punaḥ punaḥ ity evaṃ vilapan rāmaḥ paridhāvan vanād vanam
english: "Ah, beloved, where have you gone? Ah, fortunate one! Ah, Sītā!" — thus lamenting again and again, Rāma ran from forest to forest.

sanskrit: kva cid udbhramate vegāt kva cid vibhramate balāt kva cin matta ivābhāti kāntān veṣaṇatatparaḥ
english: Somewhere he rushed forward with frantic speed, somewhere he staggered uncontrollably, and somewhere he appeared like a madman, intent on searching for his beloved.

sanskrit: sa vanāni nadīḥ śailān giriprasravaṇāni ca kānanāni ca vegena bhramaty aparisaṃsthitaḥ
english: Unstable and unsettled, he wandered swiftly through forests, rivers, mountains, mountain torrents, and groves.

sanskrit: tathā sa gatvā vipulaṃ mahad vanaṃ parītya sarvaṃ tv atha maithilīṃ prati aniṣṭhitāśaḥ sa cakāra mārgaṇe punaḥ priyāyāḥ paramaṃ pariśramam
english: Having gone thus through the vast great forest and searched it all, yet finding no certainty regarding Maithilī, he made the utmost effort in searching for his beloved once again.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭāśramapadaṃ śūnyaṃ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ rahitāṃ parṇaśālāṃ ca vidhvastāny āsanāni ca
english: Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, had seen the āśrama site empty, the leaf hut deserted, and the seats scattered in disarray.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭvā tatra vaidehīṃ saṃnirīkṣya ca sarvaśaḥ uvāca rāmaḥ prākruśya pragṛhya rucirau bhujau
english: Not seeing the Vaidehi there and having surveyed everything carefully, Rāma cried out and raised his beautiful arms in lamentation, and spoke.

sanskrit: kva nu lakṣmaṇa vaidehī kaṃ vā deśam ito gatā kenāhṛtā vā saumitre bhakṣitā kena vā priyā
english: "Where has the Vaidehi gone, Lakṣmaṇa? To what place has she departed from here? By whom has she been carried off, O Saumitri, or by whom has my beloved been devoured?"

sanskrit: vṛṣkeṇāvārya yadi māṃ sīte hasitum icchasi alaṃ te hasitenādya māṃ bhajasva suduḥkhitam
english: "Sītā, if you wish to laugh at me by hiding behind that tree, enough with laughter — come to me now, for I am overwhelmed with grief."

sanskrit: yaiḥ saha krīḍase sīte viśvastair mṛgapotakaiḥ ete hīnās tvayā saumye dhyāyanty asrāvilekṣaṇāḥ
english: "Sītā, the trusting fawns with whom you used to play — these, left behind by you, O gentle one, now stand lost in thought with tear-filled eyes."

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śokena mahatā sītāharaṇajena mām paraloke mahārājo nūnaṃ drakṣyati me pitā
english: "My father the great king will surely see me in the next world, slain by this immense grief born of Sītā's abduction."

sanskrit: kathaṃ pratijñāṃ saṃśrutya mayā tvam abhiyojitaḥ apūrayitvā taṃ kālaṃ matsakāśam ihāgataḥ
english: "How is it that you, having accepted a promise from me, have come back to my presence without fulfilling the appointed time?"

sanskrit: kāmavṛttam anāryaṃ māṃ mṛṣāvādinam eva ca dhik tvām iti pare loke vyaktaṃ vakṣyati me pitā
english: "'Shame on you,' my father will surely say to me in the next world, 'you who acted from mere desire, who are ignoble, who are a speaker of false words.'"

sanskrit: vivaśaṃ śokasaṃtaptaṃ dīnaṃ bhagnamanoratham mām ihotsṛjya karuṇaṃ kīrtir naram ivānṛjum
english: "Fame has abandoned me here — helpless, scorched by grief, wretched, and broken in spirit — as if I were a dishonest man abandoned by glory."

sanskrit: kva gacchasi varārohe mām utsṛjya sumadhyame tvayā virahitaś cāhaṃ mokṣye jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: "Where are you going, O fair-hipped, slender-waisted one, leaving me behind? Separated from you, I shall give up my very life."

sanskrit: itīva vilapan rāmaḥ sītādarśanalālasaḥ na dadarśa suduḥkhārto rāghavo janakātmajām
english: Thus lamenting, and longing to see Sītā, Rāma the Rāghava, afflicted by the most severe grief, could not find the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: anāsādayamānaṃ taṃ sītāṃ daśarathātmajam paṅkam āsādya vipulaṃ sīdantam iva kuñjaram lakṣmaṇo rāmam atyartham uvāca hitakāmyayā
english: Seeing Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, unable to find Sītā and sinking like a great elephant that has reached deep mire, Lakṣmaṇa spoke to him with exceeding earnestness, out of a desire for his welfare.

sanskrit: mā viṣādaṃ mahābāho kuru yatnaṃ mayā saha idaṃ ca hi vanaṃ śūra bahukandaraśobhitam
english: "Do not despair, O mighty-armed one — make effort together with me. This forest, O hero, is adorned with many mountain caverns."

sanskrit: priyakānanasaṃcārā vanonmattā ca maithilī sā vanaṃ vā praviṣṭā syān nalinīṃ vā supuṣpitām
english: "Maithilī, who loves to roam the forest and becomes intoxicated by it, may have entered the forest or gone to a well-flowering lotus grove."

sanskrit: saritaṃ vāpi saṃprāptā mīnavañjurasevitām vitrāsayitukāmā vā līnā syāt kānane kva cit jijñāsamānā vaidehī tvāṃ māṃ ca puruṣarṣabha
english: "Or she may have reached a river frequented by fish and cranes; or the Vaidehi, wishing to startle us, O bull among men, may be hiding somewhere in the forest, curious to know where you and I are."

sanskrit: tasyā hy anveṣaṇe śrīman kṣipram eva yatāvahe vanaṃ sarvaṃ vicinuvo yatra sā janakātmajā manyase yadi kākutstha mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "Let us swiftly make effort, O glorious one, to search for her — let us two search the entire forest where the daughter of Janaka might be. If you agree, O Kākutstha, do not let your mind dwell in sorrow."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sauhārdāl lakṣmaṇena samāhitaḥ saha saumitriṇā rāmo vicetum upacakrame tau vanāni girīṃś caiva saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca
english: Thus spoken to with affection by Lakṣmaṇa and steadied by it, Rāma set out together with Saumitri to search; the two of them began to search through forests, mountains, rivers, and lakes.

sanskrit: nikhilena vicinvantau sītāṃ daśarathātmajau tasya śailasya sānūni guhāś ca śikharāṇi ca
english: The two sons of Daśaratha searched thoroughly for Sītā — the slopes of that mountain, its caves and its peaks.

sanskrit: nikhilena vicinvantau naiva tām abhijagmatuḥ vicitya sarvataḥ śailaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Though they searched thoroughly, they did not find her. Having searched the mountain in every direction, Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: neha paśyāmi saumitre vaidehīṃ parvate śubhe tato duḥkhābhisaṃtapto lakṣmaṇo vākyam abravīt
english: "I do not see the Vaidehi here on this lovely mountain, O Saumitri." Then Lakṣmaṇa, overcome with grief, spoke these words.

sanskrit: vicaran daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ bhrātaraṃ dīptatejasaṃ prāpsyasi tvaṃ mahāprājña maithilīṃ janakātmajām
english: "Wandering through the Daṇḍaka forest, O greatly wise one, you will find Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka — that blazing-spirited brother of yours awaits."

sanskrit: yathā viṣṇur mahābāhur baliṃ baddhvā mahīm imām evam uktas tu vīreṇa lakṣmaṇena sa rāghavaḥ
english: "Just as mighty-armed Viṣṇu having bound Bali recovered this earth" — thus spoken to by the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, that Rāghava —

sanskrit: uvāca dīnayā vācā duḥkhābhihatacetanaḥ vanaṃ sarvaṃ suvicitaṃ padminyaḥ phullapaṅkajāḥ
english: — spoke in a piteous voice, his mind crushed by sorrow: "The entire forest has been well searched, the lotus ponds with their blooming lotuses —"

sanskrit: giriś cāyaṃ mahāprājña bahukandaranirjharaḥ na hi paśyāmi vaidehīṃ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm
english: "— and this mountain, O greatly wise one, with its many caves and cascades; yet I do not see the Vaidehi who is dearer to me than life."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vilapan rāmaḥ sītāharaṇakarśitaḥ dīnaḥ śokasamāviṣṭo muhūrtaṃ vihvalo 'bhavat
english: Thus lamenting, Rāma, emaciated by the abduction of Sītā, wretched and utterly consumed by grief, became bewildered for a moment.

sanskrit: sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo gatabuddhir vicetanaḥ viṣasādāturo dīno niḥśvasyāśītam āyatam
english: With every limb trembling, his intellect gone, his senses absent, he sank down in distress, miserable, heaving long and cold sighs.

sanskrit: bahuśaḥ sa tu niḥśvasya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ hā priyeti vicukrośa bahuśo bāṣpagadgadaḥ
english: Sighing deeply many times, lotus-eyed Rāma cried out many times, "Ah, my beloved!" his voice choked with tears.

sanskrit: taṃ sāntvayām āsa tato lakṣmaṇaḥ priyabāndhavaḥ bahuprakāraṃ dharmajñaḥ praśritaḥ praśritāñjaliḥ
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, the dear kinsman, versed in dharma, with humility and folded hands, consoled him in many ways.

sanskrit: anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇauṣṭhapuṭacyutam apaśyaṃs tāṃ priyāṃ sītāṃ prākrośat sa punaḥ punaḥ
english: But disregarding those words that had fallen from Lakṣmaṇa's lips, not seeing his beloved Sītā, he cried out again and again.

sanskrit: sa dīno dīnayā vācā lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt śīghraṃ lakṣmaṇa jānīhi gatvā godāvarīṃ nadīm api godāvarīṃ sītā padmāny ānayituṃ gatā
english: Wretched, in a wretched voice he spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa: "Go quickly, Lakṣmaṇa, and find out what has become of the river Godāvarī — perhaps Sītā has gone to the Godāvarī to bring back lotuses."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ punar eva hi nadīṃ godāvarīṃ ramyāṃ jagāma laghuvikramaḥ
english: Thus spoken to by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, swift in his movements, went once again to the lovely river Godāvarī.

sanskrit: tāṃ lakṣmaṇas tīrthavatīṃ vicitvā rāmam abravīt naināṃ paśyāmi tīrtheṣu krośato na śṛṇoti me
english: Having searched that river with its many fords, Lakṣmaṇa spoke to Rāma: "I do not see her at the fords; she does not hear me even when I call out."

sanskrit: kaṃ nu sā deśam āpannā vaidehī kleśanāśinī na hi taṃ vedmi vai rāma yatra sā tanumadhyamā
english: "What place has the Vaidehi, the destroyer of sorrow, reached? I do not know, O Rāma, where that slender-waisted one has gone."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā dīnaḥ saṃtāpa mohitaḥ rāmaḥ samabhicakrāma svayaṃ godāvarīṃ nadīm
english: Hearing Lakṣmaṇa's words, wretched and bewildered by anguish, Rāma himself proceeded to the river Godāvarī.

sanskrit: sa tām upasthito rāmaḥ kva sītety evam abravīt
english: Approaching her, Rāma spoke thus: "Where is Sītā?"

sanskrit: bhūtāni rākṣasendreṇa vadhārheṇa hṛtām api na tāṃ śaśaṃsū rāmāya tathā godāvarī nadī
english: Neither the beings dwelling there, nor the river Godāvarī, revealed to Rāma that she had been carried off by the lord of rākṣasas who deserves to be slain.

sanskrit: tataḥ pracoditā bhūtaiḥ śaṃsāsmai tāṃ priyām iti na ca sābhyavadat sītāṃ pṛṣṭā rāmeṇa śocitā
english: Then, though the beings urged her, "Tell him about his beloved," yet she, when questioned by Rāma, did not disclose Sītā's whereabouts, being filled with grief.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya ca tad rūpaṃ karmāṇi ca durātmanaḥ dhyātvā bhayāt tu vaidehīṃ sā nadī na śaśaṃsa tām
english: Reflecting on the form and the deeds of that wicked-souled Rāvaṇa, the river, out of fear, did not reveal the Vaidehi's fate.

sanskrit: nirāśas tu tayā nadyā sītāyā darśane kṛtaḥ uvāca rāmaḥ saumitriṃ sītādarśanakarśitaḥ
english: Made hopeless by that river of ever seeing Sītā, Rāma, emaciated by his longing to see Sītā, spoke to Saumitri.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu lakṣmaṇa vakṣyāmi sametya janakaṃ vacaḥ mātaraṃ caiva vaidehyā vinā tām aham apriyam
english: "What words shall I say, O Lakṣmaṇa, when I meet Janaka and the mother of the Vaidehi, without her — what unpleasant news shall I bring?"

sanskrit: yā me rājyavihīnasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ sarvaṃ vyapanayac chokaṃ vaidehī kva nu sā gatā
english: "She who removed all my grief as I lived in the forest on forest fare, deprived of my kingdom — where now has that Vaidehi gone?"

sanskrit: jñātipakṣavihīnasya rājaputrīm apaśyataḥ manye dīrghā bhaviṣyanti rātrayo mama jāgrataḥ
english: "For me, bereft of my kinsmen's side and not seeing the princess, the nights will be long indeed, I think, as I lie awake."

sanskrit: godāvarīṃ janasthānam imaṃ prasravaṇaṃ girim sarvāṇy anucariṣyāmi yadi sītā hi dṛśyate
english: "I shall roam through the Godāvarī, this Janasthāna, and this mountain with its cascades — all of them — if only Sītā might be found."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇau tāv anyonyaṃ bhrātarāv ubhau vasuṃdharāyāṃ patitaṃ puṣpamārgam apaśyatām
english: As the two brothers were thus conversing with one another, they noticed on the ground a trail of scattered flowers.

sanskrit: tāṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahītale uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vīro duḥkhito duḥkhitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing that shower of flowers fallen on the earth, the heroic Rāma, grieving, spoke these grievous words to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: abhijānāmi puṣpāṇi tānīmāmīha lakṣmaṇa apinaddhāni vaidehyā mayā dattāni kānane
english: "I recognize these flowers here, Lakṣmaṇa — the ones that had been worn upon the Vaidehi's body, given by me in the forest."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur lakṣmaṇaṃ puruṣarṣabham kruddho 'bravīd giriṃ tatra siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: Having said this, the mighty-armed one, that bull among men, spoke in fury to the mountain there, like a lion addressing a small deer.

sanskrit: tāṃ hemavarṇāṃ hemābhāṃ sītāṃ darśaya parvata yāvat sānūni sarvāṇi na te vidhvaṃsayāmy aham
english: "Show me Sītā, O mountain, she of golden hue and golden radiance — before I shatter all your slopes to ruin."

sanskrit: mama bāṇāgninirdagdho bhasmībhūto bhaviṣyasi asevyaḥ satataṃ caiva nistṛṇadrumapallavaḥ
english: "Scorched by the fire of my arrows, you will be reduced to ash, forever inaccessible, stripped of grass, trees, and foliage."

sanskrit: imāṃ vā saritaṃ cādya śoṣayiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa yadi nākhyāti me sītām adya candranibhānanām
english: "Or today I shall dry up this river as well, Lakṣmaṇa, if she does not reveal to me today Sītā of the moon-like face."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa ruṣito rāmo didhakṣann iva cakṣuṣā dadarśa bhūmau niṣkrāntaṃ rākṣasasya padaṃ mahat
english: Thus enraged, with eyes blazing as though to set fire to everything, Rāma saw on the ground a great footprint left by the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: sa samīkṣya parikrāntaṃ sītāyā rākṣasasya ca saṃbhrāntahṛdayo rāmaḥ śaśaṃsa bhrātaraṃ priyam
english: Seeing the tracks of Sītā and the rākṣasa, Rāma, his heart seized with agitation, told his dear brother.

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ śīrṇāḥ kanakabindavaḥ bhūṣaṇānāṃ hi saumitre mālyāni vividhāni ca
english: "Look, Lakṣmaṇa — the scattered gold droplets from the Vaidehi's ornaments, O Saumitri, and various garlands as well."

sanskrit: taptabindunikāśaiś ca citraiḥ kṣatajabindubhiḥ āvṛtaṃ paśya saumitre sarvato dharaṇītalam
english: "Look, O Saumitri — the ground everywhere is covered with bright drops of blood like glowing molten metal."

sanskrit: manye lakṣmaṇa vaidehī rākṣasaiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ bhittvā bhittvā vibhaktā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati
english: "I think, Lakṣmaṇa, that the Vaidehi has been torn limb from limb and dismembered, or devoured, by the shape-shifting rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tasya nimittaṃ vaidehyā dvayor vivadamānayoḥ babhūva yuddhaṃ saumitre ghoraṃ rākṣasayor iha
english: "For the sake of the Vaidehi, there must have been a terrible battle here between two rākṣasas who were quarreling, O Saumitri."

sanskrit: muktāmaṇicitaṃ cedaṃ tapanīyavibhūṣitam dharaṇyāṃ patitaṃ saumya kasya bhagnaṃ mahad dhanuḥ
english: "Whose great bow is this, inlaid with pearls and gems, adorned with refined gold, lying broken on the ground, O gentle one?"

sanskrit: taruṇādityasaṃkāśaṃ vaidūryagulikācitam viśīrṇaṃ patitaṃ bhūmau kavacaṃ kasya kāñcanam
english: "Whose is this golden armour, radiant as the young sun, set with beryl globes, shattered and fallen to the earth?"

sanskrit: chatraṃ śataśalākaṃ ca divyamālyopaśobhitam bhagnadaṇḍam idaṃ kasya bhūmau saumya nipātitam
english: "Whose royal parasol, with its hundred ribs, adorned with divine garlands, its handle broken, has been cast down to the earth, O gentle one?"

sanskrit: kāñcanoraśchadāś ceme piśācavadanāḥ kharāḥ bhīmarūpā mahākāyāḥ kasya vā nihatā raṇe
english: "And these donkeys with golden chest-coverings, with the faces of piśācas, of fearsome form and massive bodies — whose are they, slain in battle?"

sanskrit: dīptapāvakasaṃkāśo dyutimān samaradhvajaḥ apaviddhaś ca bhagnaś ca kasya sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ
english: "Whose war chariot, brilliant as blazing fire, resplendent with its battle-standard, has been hurled away and broken?"

sanskrit: rathākṣamātrā viśikhās tapanīyavibhūṣaṇāḥ kasyeme 'bhihatā bāṇāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ
english: "Whose are these terrible arrows, as long as a chariot axle, adorned with refined gold, that lie scattered about after striking their mark?"

sanskrit: vairaṃ śataguṇaṃ paśya mamedaṃ jīvitāntakam sughorahṛdayaiḥ saumya rākṣasaiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
english: "Look at this enmity against me, a hundredfold, lethal to my very life, O gentle one — wrought by those shape-shifting rākṣasas of utterly vile hearts."

sanskrit: hṛtā mṛtā vā sītā hi bhakṣitā vā tapasvinī na dharmas trāyate sītāṃ hriyamāṇāṃ mahāvane
english: "Sītā the ascetic has been abducted, or killed, or devoured — dharma did not protect Sītā as she was being carried off in this great forest."

sanskrit: bhakṣitāyāṃ hi vaidehyāṃ hṛtāyām api lakṣmaṇa ke hi loke priyaṃ kartuṃ śaktāḥ saumya mameśvarāḥ
english: "With the Vaidehi devoured or even abducted, O Lakṣmaṇa, O gentle one — what lords in this world are capable of doing something dear to me?"

sanskrit: kartāram api lokānāṃ śūraṃ karuṇavedinam ajñānād avamanyeran sarvabhūtāni lakṣmaṇa
english: "All beings, O Lakṣmaṇa, shall disrespect out of ignorance even the creator of worlds, even one who is heroic and compassionate."

sanskrit: mṛduṃ lokahite yuktaṃ dāntaṃ karuṇavedinam nirvīrya iti manyante nūnaṃ māṃ tridaśeśvarāḥ
english: "Surely the lords of the thirty gods consider me, who am gentle, devoted to the welfare of the world, self-restrained, and compassionate, to be devoid of heroism."

sanskrit: māṃ prāpya hi guṇo doṣaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ paśya lakṣmaṇa adyaiva sarvabhūtānāṃ rakṣasām abhavāya ca saṃhṛtyaiva śaśijyotsnāṃ mahān sūrya ivoditaḥ
english: "A virtue has turned into a fault upon meeting with me — look, Lakṣmaṇa: today, withdrawing the moonlight as a great sun rises, I shall arise for the destruction of all beings and rākṣasas alike."

sanskrit: naiva yakṣā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ kiṃnarā vā manuṣyā vā sukhaṃ prāpsyanti lakṣmaṇa
english: "Neither yakṣas, nor gandharvas, nor piśācas, nor rākṣasas, nor kiṃnaras, nor human beings shall find happiness, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: mamāstrabāṇasaṃpūrṇam ākāśaṃ paśya lakṣmaṇa niḥsaṃpātaṃ kariṣyāmi hy adya trailokyacāriṇām
english: "Look, Lakṣmaṇa — today I shall fill the sky with my weapons and arrows, making it impassable for those who travel through the three worlds."

sanskrit: saṃniruddhagrahagaṇam āvāritaniśākaram vipranaṣṭānalamarudbhāskaradyutisaṃvṛtam
english: "With the host of planets blocked off, the moon obstructed, the light of fire, wind, and sun extinguished and covered over —"

sanskrit: vinirmathitaśailāgraṃ śuṣyamāṇajalāśayam dhvastadrumalatāgulmaṃ vipraṇāśitasāgaram
english: "— with mountain peaks shattered, water-bodies drying up, trees, creepers and shrubs destroyed, the oceans obliterated —"

sanskrit: na tāṃ kuśalinīṃ sītāṃ pradāsyanti mameśvarāḥ asmin muhūrte saumitre mama drakṣyanti vikramam
english: "If the lords do not restore to me Sītā safe and well, this very moment, O Saumitri, they shall witness my might."

sanskrit: nākāśam utpatiṣyanti sarvabhūtāni lakṣmaṇa mama cāpaguṇān muktair bāṇajālair nirantaram
english: "No creature shall fly through the sky, O Lakṣmaṇa, under the unceasing torrents of arrows released from my bowstring."

sanskrit: arditaṃ mama nārācair dhvastabhrāntamṛgadvijam samākulam amaryādaṃ jagat paśyādya lakṣmaṇa
english: "Look today, O Lakṣmaṇa, at the universe tormented by my iron arrows, its roaming deer and birds destroyed, thrown into chaos and stripped of all bounds."

sanskrit: ākarṇapūrṇair iṣubhir jīvalokaṃ durāvaraiḥ kariṣye maithilīhetor apiśācam arākṣasaṃ
english: "With arrows drawn to the ear, arrows that are hard to resist, I shall reduce the world of the living, for Maithilī's sake, to one without piśācas and without rākṣasas."

sanskrit: mama roṣaprayuktānāṃ sāyakānāṃ balaṃ surāḥ drakṣyanty adya vimuktānām amarṣād dūragāminām
english: "Today the gods shall witness the power of my arrows, loosed by my fury, discharged in wrath, flying far."

sanskrit: naiva devā na daiteyā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ bhaviṣyanti mama krodhāt trailokye vipraṇāśite
english: "Neither gods, nor daityas, nor piśācas, nor rākṣasas shall exist once the three worlds are annihilated by my wrath."

sanskrit: devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ lokā ye rakṣasām api bahudhā nipatiṣyanti bāṇaughaiḥ śakulīkṛtāḥ nirmaryādān imāṃl lokān kariṣyāmy adya sāyakaiḥ
english: "The worlds of gods, dānavas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas alike shall fall down in many pieces, ripped apart by floods of arrows; today with my shafts I shall make these worlds lawless."

sanskrit: yathā jarā yathā mṛtyur yathākālo yathāvidhiḥ nityaṃ na pratihanyante sarvabhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa tathāhaṃ krodhasaṃyukto na nivāryo 'smy asaṃśayam
english: "Just as old age, death, time, and fate are never obstructed among all beings, O Lakṣmaṇa — so I, filled with fury, am beyond all restraint, without doubt."

sanskrit: pureva me cārudatīm aninditāṃ diśanti sītāṃ yadi nādya maithilīm sadevagandharvamanuṣya pannagaṃ jagat saśailaṃ parivartayāmy aham
english: "If they do not restore to me today Maithilī, that blameless one of lovely teeth, as they did before, I shall overturn the entire world with its gods, gandharvas, humans, serpents, and mountains."
